extracted.intended_audience: Prospective predoctoral and postdoctoral fellowship applicants (F30, F31, F32), sponsors, and institutional administrators
extracted.subtask_description: NICHD-specific FAQ guidance on eligibility, allowable activities, administrative requirements, and benefits for individual NRSA fellowships (F30, F31, F32). Includes rules for foreign training, transfers, leave, supplementation, and stipend/tax treatment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of NRSA fellowship support and benefits
rubrics_metrics.description: NICHD participates in the Parent F30 Fellowship for dual-degree students, the Parent F31 Predoctoral Fellowship program, and the F32 Individual Postdoctoral Fellowship program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These fellowships provide stipends for salary support as well as a small institutional allowance to partially offset costs of research, tuition, and health insurance. Predoctoral and postdoctoral fellows can also receive support on slots (FTEs) awarded to an Institutional Training Grant (T32).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific fit with NICHD mission
rubrics_metrics.description: Prospective applicants are strongly advised to contact the NICHD to determine if their research fits within the NICHD mission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NICHD offers fellowships and career development awards in research areas relevant to the institute's scientific priorities; applicants should consult NICHD program staff to confirm fit before applying.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citizenship/residency eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Foreign students are not eligible for NRSA fellowships.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: By the time of an F31 or F32 award, the individual must be a citizen or a non-citizen national of the United States or have been lawfully admitted for permanent residence (i.e., possess a currently valid Permanent Resident Card USCIS Form I-551, or other legal verification of such status). See the specific program announcement for more information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign training for postdoctoral fellows — allowability and clearance
rubrics_metrics.description: Foreign training for postdoctoral fellows is allowable but foreign clearance from the Fogarty International Center is needed prior to award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fellowship applicants must provide detailed justification for the foreign training, including why facilities, the mentor, or other aspects are more appropriate than domestic training. Foreign training may require additional administrative reviews and will be considered for funding only when the scientific advantages are clear (GPS Section 11.2.2.5).

rubrics_metrics.name: Review considerations for applications involving foreign training
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications involving foreign training are considered by reviewers under 'Additional Review Considerations,' which do not receive scores and do not enter into the overall impact/priority score.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For applications from foreign sponsoring institutions, reviewers will assess whether the research training experience presents special opportunities for the fellowship applicant through use of talent (e.g., mentor), populations, or training environment not readily available in the United States or that augment existing U.S. talent/resources (GPS Section 11.2.4.4).

rubrics_metrics.name: Travel allowance for foreign training sites
rubrics_metrics.description: For fellows at foreign training sites, awards may include a single economy or coach round-trip travel fare; no allowance is provided for dependents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: U.S. flag air carriers must be used to the maximum extent possible when commercial air transportation is the means of travel between the United States and a foreign country or between foreign countries. Any funds awarded for travel to/from foreign training sites must be reported on the Termination Notice as part of the 'Amount of Stipend' column.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional/site change expectations for postdoctoral training
rubrics_metrics.description: In most cases, the sponsoring institution should be a site other than where the applicant fellow trained as a graduate student.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the applicant proposes postdoctoral training at his/her doctoral institution, the application must carefully document the opportunities for new research training experiences specifically designed to broaden scientific background and to acquire new knowledge and/or technical skills to become an independent investigator.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuation of fellowship with faculty appointment
rubrics_metrics.description: An NRSA postdoctoral fellow receiving an appointment as a clinical instructor or other faculty position would probably not be able to continue under F32 support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At time of award, individuals are required to pursue research training on a full-time basis, normally defined as 40 hours per week. Any new faculty appointment would normally involve duties not considered postdoctoral research training. NRSA fellowships may not be used to support the clinical years of residency training; they are appropriate for research fellowship years only. Approval is required for transfer of the award to another institution, change in sponsor, or project change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transfers, changes in sponsor, and project changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Individual fellowship awards are made for training at a specific institution under the guidance of a particular sponsor; approval of the NIH awarding IC is required for a transfer of the award to another institution, a change in sponsor, or a project change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a fellow requests a transfer to another domestic non-Federal institution before the end of the current award year, institutions must negotiate which will pay the stipend until year-end; disposition of the institutional allowance is negotiable. Transfers involving Federal or foreign sponsoring institutions require unique administrative procedures and approvals. Any proposed change in specified area of research training must be reviewed/approved in writing by the NIH awarding IC. When the sponsor will be absent for more than 3 continuous months, an interim sponsor must be named and approved in writing by the NIH awarding IC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leave and parental leave policy
rubrics_metrics.description: NRSA fellowship recipients are entitled to 15 days of sick leave per year, and up to 60 calendar days of parental leave; the NRSA stipend will continue during those periods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The fellow may take an unpaid leave of absence if more than 60 days off are expected. No NRSA funds can be spent during the unpaid leave period, though health insurance coverage may be continued by the institution. Institutional allowance or other NRSA funds may not be used during unpaid leave. The overall award period would be extended to offset the duration of the unpaid leave (Grants Policy Statement Section 11.2.13.1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementation rules (raising stipend)
rubrics_metrics.description: Supplementation is extra salary support provided to an NRSA fellow to raise the rate above the standard NRSA stipend scale; such supplementation cannot be derived from Public Health Service funds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any supplementation must be provided to all students in a particular program (i.e., all predoctoral or postdoctoral trainees appointed to the slots). A T32 program director cannot supplement the stipend of just one trainee. Applications for supplements must be submitted by the Principal Investigator of the parent (existing) grant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compensation vs. supplementation (employment while a fellow)
rubrics_metrics.description: Compensation is salary paid to an individual in a formal employee-employer relationship (e.g., teaching assistant, research assistant).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compensation may come from NIH grant funds, but it cannot be from a grant that is already part of the trainee's research training experience, and it cannot detract from or delay progress on the proposed training program. NIH usually uses 25% time (equivalent to 10 hours per week) as the maximum commitment on employment for compensation. Employment should be restricted to activities that enhance the trainee's professional skill set.

rubrics_metrics.name: Full-time professional effort requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: NRSA program requires full-time professional effort, normally defined as 40 hours per week.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fellows are expected to devote full-time to their proposed research training; clinical duties must be confined to activities that are part of the research training program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tax status and employment classification of stipend recipients
rubrics_metrics.description: An NRSA stipend is provided by the NIH as a subsistence allowance; NRSA recipients are not considered employees of the federal government or the grantee institution for purposes of the award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIH takes no position on the status of a particular taxpayer or on tax law interpretation; the Internal Revenue Service determines tax treatment. Questions about income taxes and social security withholding should be directed to tax authorities.
